en: The Warden of Ansedra's water, who keeps the lagoon flat and the barges poled. He read the declaration in a clear voice and believed every word of it. The flat-engine on his barge stills the water in its wake.
Take your places in the gallery. The vows are at dusk.
To the barge. Get through the water-gate.
A hull-captain needs someone who may go up to the dais.
Hold the steps until Merel cuts the barge loose.
The flat-engine slows you with every pulse. Liss can break it.
The Order's shrines won't answer you now. The Kirru and the Saltwrights keep shrines of their own, and those still do.
A flake of the Lacquer Court's red, broken off in the fighting. Used in Customize.
A wright's lamp with a crack across the glass, carried in a padded box. Liss won't let anyone else hold the box.
Wrist-guards lacquered the court's red. She wore them to the wedding.
A black lacquer drum on the stern of the Warden's barge, with a fan of eight paddles that press the lagoon flat. A steady teal light burns in its window.
Liss stays in: only she can reach the engine's works.
Only Liss can reach the engine's works.
Stillguard in the court's wedding lacquer, sent down the water-steps when the Conclave sprang its trap. They are as patient as the water they keep.
Kerrid holds the steps: he stays in until the barge is loose.
